verdicts.trueWording: actually detract slightly from the antithesis of bread and stone
verdicts.note: Raw PDF (pdftotext -layout), p.15 (page header 'New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin 15'). Sentence runs 'But the closing clauses, rhythmically necessary, actually detract slightly from' + next line 'the antithesis of bread and stone, and the entirely homely simile.' The preceding block quote is the love/bread/stone passage cited to Lathe of Heaven p.136; running head confirms Sylvia A. Kelso as author. Every limb (Kelso, Lathe, closing clauses, rhythmically necessary, weakened antithesis and homely simile) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: As of the date of this report the Seggri have not
verdicts.note: Raw HTML from sfsfss.com. In the closing historical/frame narration after Merriment's departure and the Iyoo/Wu mission: the sentence continues 'undertaken major genetic alteration'. No calendar year is attached anywhere in that frame paragraph, so the self-dating limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: They made Resehavanar's Choice as "all the truth slowly."
verdicts.note: Raw page, same closing frame paragraph (immediately before the 'As of the date of this report' sentence). Capitalised proper term, no definition offered in the frame; the term also appears twice inside the Mobile's field notes ('we are facing Resehavanar's Choice here'; 'I chose the option: Less than the truth'), which is where the procedure's options are implied - the frame itself never explains it, so the 'unglossed' limb stands as claimed.

verdicts.trueWording: They are ordinary drudges, living in towns which belong
verdicts.note: Raw page, under the heading 'CAPTAIN AOLAO-OLAO'S REPORT'. Archaic register in the same section: 'consonant with their unregenerate state', 'They evinced great fear', 'it were best for us'. The frame/editorial narrator elsewhere writes plain modern prose (e.g. the 'As of the date of this report' paragraph), supporting the contrast limb.

Quote is verbatim in the closing autobiographical sketch, and the application limb is supported ('as part of my application to return to Seggri as a Mobile of the Ekumen'). But the memoir does not END there: the filing formula sits three sentences from the close, and the last sentence is reflective, ending on knowing 'with at least an uncertain certainty who I am'. Confirmed against the tail of the raw file.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: ends on a filing formula - the formula is mid-paragraph; the memoir's final sentence is reflective, not bureaucratic

verdicts.trueWording: the final section, some 100 pages, called
verdicts.note: Raw blogspot HTML; byline 'by Rich Horton', blog masthead 'Strange at Ecbatan', dated Wednesday, April 24, 2024. Sentence: it seemed a case of a writer including her study notes '(And, to be sure, she literally does -- in the final section, some 100 pages, called "The Back of the Book"...)'. The page's own label for the closing section is The Back of the Book; Horton's final paragraph calls the same material 'ethnographic'.

verdicts.trueWording: intellectually intriguing, but, really, often a struggle to read
verdicts.note: Raw page, final-verdict paragraph beginning 'What's my final verdict?'. Subject is 'The ethnographic bits -- and they are not just "bits"'. Claim's 'intellectually interesting' paraphrases the page's 'intriguing'; 'hard to read' matches 'a struggle to read'.

verdicts.trueWording: like a writer deciding to include all her notes
verdicts.note: Raw page, paragraph beginning 'But no longer!': 'It does read, to a great extent, like a writer deciding to include all her notes.' The deliberateness limb is carried by the next sentence, in which Horton says he is certain Le Guin did this with full intention.

verdicts.trueWording: The encyclopedic form of Always Coming Home
verdicts.note: Raw loa.org page. The sentence ('...was exactly what she needed at the time, to do the job she wanted to do') closes the answer prefixed 'Attebery:' about nonlinear form; the intro paragraph identifies 'The editor of the new LOA volume is Brian Attebery'. Note the quoted line is the fourth Q&A block, not the third answer as the claim's page field says - a locator slip, not a claim limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin's mode is ethnography, not epic.
verdicts.note: Raw reactormag.com page; byline 'By Matthew Keeley'. Closes the paragraph beginning 'The interrupted story which resumes 150 pages later', which contrasts the novelistic Stone Telling narrative with an anthropologist's carrier bag of documents.

verdicts.trueWording: where those who want narrative can ignore them
verdicts.note: Same raw Reactor page, paragraph beginning 'The table of contents for this book is several pages long'. Keeley reports that the author announces on the first page that some of the more explanatory, descriptive pieces are relegated to The Back of the Book, with the quoted clause plus 'and those who enjoy explanations can find them.' First-page, set-apart and skippable limbs all present.

verdicts.trueWording: To me the style is the book, to a large extent
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (20140118190325id_) of the Paris Review interview; header 'Ursula K. Le Guin, The Art of Fiction No. 221 / Interviewed by John Wray'. Sentence sits in a block prefixed 'LE GUIN' about idea-writers who scorned style, and continues 'Take Borges.', matching the claim's locator.

verdicts.trueWording: Showing can be quite static, after all
verdicts.note: Raw ursulakleguin.com page, Session 1. Full sentence: the quoted clause then '; but telling always involves moving on.' It closes the reply prefixed 'UKL :' to the questioner named Paige, whose question is the show-don't-tell one.

verdicts.trueWording: reflection and action, character and action, are not opposites
verdicts.note: Raw ursulakleguin.com page, Session 1 Continued, under the heading 'SOME FALSE DICHOTOMIES', in a reply prefixed 'Ursula :'. On the page the clause is preceded by 'Above all,' and followed by an exclamation mark, then 'What people do arises from what they think and who they are.'

verdicts.trueWording: neither is an obligatory ingredient of narrative
verdicts.note: Same raw page and 'SOME FALSE DICHOTOMIES' section, same paragraph as index 527: conflict is called one possible element of a story, intense suspensefulness another, and then the quoted clause. Both limbs of the claim are on the page.
